ラピダス(Rapidus).short: Rapidus is a semiconductor manufacturer that aims to mass-produce leading-edge 2 nm-generation logic chips in Japan. It began prototyping at its fab in Chitose, Hokkaido, in 2025 and plans to start volume production in 2027.
why: Started operating the pilot line at IIM-1, its fab in Chitose, Hokkaido.
Announced that 2 nm-generation GAA transistors prototyped at IIM-1 had been confirmed to work electrically.
Announced that it had raised a total of 267.6 billion yen from the government and private companies.
Opened Rapidus Chiplet Solutions, which handles the design and manufacture of chiplets and packages, and an analysis center in Chitose.
Announced Rapidus CORE, a framework for supporting customer designs, and named 17 design companies as its first partners.
ラピダス(Rapidus).background: As a national project to build a volume fab for leading-edge logic chips in Japan, its fab progress, fundraising and customer wins are reported frequently.
ラピダス(Rapidus).diff: Fabs also widely use batch processing, which treats many wafers together in steps such as thermal treatment and cleaning. Rapidus runs its entire front end as single-wafer processing, one wafer at a time, and promotes a business model (RUMS) that links design, front-end and back-end processing in a short time, aiming to make a short manufacturing turnaround time (TAT) its strength. The industry's division of labour between foundries, fabless companies and IDMs is explained on the foundry glossary page.

チップレット.short: Chiplets are a way of building a product from small chips split up by function and connected inside one package, instead of one large chip. Because they help with yield and cost, they are used in AI processors and PC CPUs.
why: Ten companies (AMD, Arm, ASE, Google Cloud, Intel, Meta, Microsoft, Qualcomm, Samsung and TSMC) announced UCIe 1.0, a standard for connecting chiplets to each other.
The UCIe industry consortium released UCIe 3.0, raising the data rate to up to 64 GT/s (twice that of UCIe 2.0).
At CES 2026, Intel announced Core Ultra Series 3 (code name Panther Lake), which combines a CPU tile made on Intel 18A with other tiles made on Intel 3 and TSMC N3E and N6.
Rapidus opened Rapidus Chiplet Solutions in Chitose, which handles the design and manufacture of chiplets and packages.
チップレット.background: Scaling alone no longer delivers easy performance gains, and the larger a chip gets, the harder yield and cost become. That has drawn attention to chiplets, which combine chips made on different processes, and to the advanced packaging that supports them.
チップレット.diff: A conventional monolithic SoC builds every function on a single piece of silicon. With chiplets, the CPU, GPU, I/O and so on become separate chips, and each can use the process that suits it. Small chips are less likely to hit a defect, so yield improves, but there is a trade-off: the power and latency of the die-to-die wiring and the complexity of the package increase.

HBM.short: HBM is memory made by stacking several DRAM dies and connecting them to the processor through a very large number of wires. It is used in AI GPUs and similar chips to read and write large amounts of data at high speed.
why: JEDEC released the next-generation standard HBM4 (JESD270-4). It doubles the interface width to 2,048 bits and specifies up to 2 TB/s of bandwidth per stack.
SK hynix announced that it had completed HBM4 development and was ready for volume production.
Samsung announced that it had begun shipping volume-production HBM4 running at 11.7 Gb/s per pin.
HBM.background: In AI training and inference, performance is often set less by the computation itself than by how fast data can be moved from memory, so HBM is indispensable for AI accelerator chips. New generations of the standard and the start of volume production at each memory maker make the news.
HBM.diff: DDR and GDDR memory run components laid out on the board at high speed over relatively few wires. HBM places DRAM stacked with TSVs right next to the processor and transfers data in parallel over many wires: 1,024 up to HBM3, and 2,048 in HBM4. The key difference is that it raises total bandwidth and power efficiency while keeping the per-pin speed modest.

GAA(ゲートオールアラウンド).label: 2nm generation (GAA transistors)
GAA(ゲートオールアラウンド).short: The 2 nm generation is where the transistor structure switches from FinFET to GAA (gate-all-around). By surrounding the channel with the gate on all sides, it keeps the current reliably switchable on and off even as devices shrink further.
why: Samsung announced that it had begun initial production of 3 nm-generation chips using GAA transistors (which it calls MBCFET).
Rapidus announced that it had prototyped 2 nm-generation GAA transistors and confirmed that they work.
TSMC began volume production of its 2 nm generation (N2), its first to use nanosheet GAA transistors.
At CES 2026, Intel announced Core Ultra Series 3 (Panther Lake), made on Intel 18A with GAA RibbonFET transistors.
GAA(ゲートオールアラウンド).background: With the major manufacturers' generations around 2 nm entering volume production one after another, the words "2nm" and "GAA" now appear often in the news. Note that "2 nm" is the name of a generation; it does not mean that any particular dimension of the transistor is exactly 2 nm.
GAA(ゲートオールアラウンド).diff: A FinFET wraps the gate around three sides of a fin-shaped channel. GAA stacks thin sheet-shaped channels (nanosheets) vertically and wraps the gate all the way around each one. Stronger gate control makes leakage current easier to suppress, and the drive current can be tuned by changing the sheet width.

裏面電源供給.label: Backside power delivery (BSPDN)
裏面電源供給.short: Backside power delivery (BSPDN) moves the power wiring that feeds the transistors to the back of the wafer. It frees the front-side wiring for signals and reduces voltage drop, and it is starting to be adopted at generations around 2 nm and beyond.
why: TSMC announced A16, which uses its "Super Power Rail" backside power delivery, and said it plans to start volume production in the second half of 2026.
Intel announced that it is manufacturing Intel 18A processors, which combine RibbonFET with PowerVia backside power delivery, at Fab 52, its fab in Arizona, USA.
At CES 2026, Intel announced Core Ultra Series 3 (Panther Lake), made on Intel 18A.
裏面電源供給.background: Until now, chips have stacked all their power and signal wiring on the front side. As scaling made the wires thinner and more crowded, voltage drop in the power supply became a serious problem, so major manufacturers announced they would adopt backside power delivery in their next generations, drawing attention to the technology.
裏面電源供給.diff: With conventional front-side power delivery, both power and signals run through the multilayer wiring above the transistors. With backside power delivery, the wafer is thinned and thick power lines are built on the back, bringing power directly close to the transistors. The shorter, wider power path reduces IR drop and frees the front-side wiring for signals. On the other hand, it adds process steps such as wafer bonding and thinning, and it changes how heat is removed.
